title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 238
paragraphs: Having said this, Xerxes went to inspect the bodies of the dead. As for Leonidas, on hearing that he had been the king and commander of the Lacedaemonians, he ordered them to cut off his head and crucify the body. It has been made clear to me by many other proofs, but by none more strongly than by this, that King Xerxes had been more enraged with Leonidas while alive than with any other man on earth; for otherwise he would never have inflicted this outrage on his corpse, since of all the men I know, the Persians are most accustomed to honor those who are good men in war. Those to whom it was appointed to do these things, then, proceeded to do so.
